paragraphs:
(Betzalel son of Uri, Exodus 31:20 as supplied [compare 31:2].)
In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, beginning of chapter 2: R' Chuna, R' Uri, R' Yosef, Rav Yehudah, in the name of Shmuel. In Derekh Eretz Rabbah, beginning of chapter 1: R' Chanina ben Uri. Hyman says that in truth the reading should be ‘R' Chuna, R' Idi,’ as in Tanchuma, Lekh Lekha 1, note 3.

notes.text: The biblical locator is printed Exodus 31:20; the earlier translation’s additional verse 2 has no source basis. The subsequent name correction is Hyman’s.

The saved whole Masorah Exodus31:2 verse explicitly names Betzalel son of Uri; it supplies the matching verse alongside supplied31:20. This does not prove a kaf/bet print or transcription substitution, nor identify biblical Uri with the rabbinic headword. The old addition2-and20 is not restored as one printed locator. רפ״ב/רפ״א mean beginning of chapters2/1, not end-of-beginning. Hyman’s IN TRUTH SHOULD READ Chuna, Idi correction retains its force and attribution; the chain and TanchumaLekh1 note3 were not newly verified. Full Rav Yehudah is supplied; other personal titles remain R'.

The 1910 printed Hyman notice gives Exodus 31:2 (שמות לא־ב), the verse that names Betzalel son of Uri. The supplied transcription reads 31:20. Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:1 has Chuna and Uri, while Buber’s printed note 3 to Tanchuma, Lekh Lekha 1, records that reading and explicitly proposes Idi for Uri. The main Tanchuma text names Rav Idi and Rav Huna. Derekh Eretz Rabbah 1:4 separately names Rabbi Chanina ben Uri in the name of Rabbi Natan.
